subject: physics
title: National and global energy resources
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: National and global energy resources — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.1.3.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering National and global energy resources, specification section 4.1.3.
final_note: You worked through National and global energy resources — 14 specification statements.

concepts.def: A supply of energy that people can draw on. The main energy resources available for use on Earth include fossil fuels (coal, oil and gas), nuclear fuel, bio-fuel, wind, hydro-electricity, geothermal, the tides, the Sun and water waves. Electricity is not an energy resource: it has to be generated using one of these resources.

The three fossil fuels named by the specification. They formed from the remains of living things over many millions of years and are burned to release energy. They are non-renewable: they are not replenished on any timescale that matters against the rate at which they are used.
Uranium (or plutonium) used as a fuel in nuclear power stations. It is mined from rock but it is not a fossil fuel, and it is non-renewable because the fuel is not replenished as it is used.
Fuel made from plant or animal material, for example wood, crops grown for fuel, or waste. It is renewable because the crops used can be grown again as the fuel is used.

Moving air, used as an energy resource mainly for electricity generation. It is renewable, and it is unreliable in the sense that its output rises and falls with the weather and cannot be turned up on demand.

An energy resource that uses water stored behind a dam, usually in a river valley. It is renewable, because rain refills the reservoir, and it is comparatively reliable because the stored water can be released when it is wanted.
An energy resource that uses the energy of hot rock beneath the Earth's surface. It is renewable and available at all hours, but it is only practical where hot rock lies close enough to the surface.

The twice-daily rise and fall of the sea, caused by the Moon and the Sun rather than by the weather. Tidal energy is renewable and reliable, because the times of high and low water are known in advance.

The Sun is an energy resource in its own right. Its energy can be used for heating (for example warming water directly) as well as for electricity generation. It is renewable, and its output varies with the time of day, the season and the cloud.
Waves on the surface of the sea, raised by the wind. Wave energy is renewable and is a separate resource from both hydro-electricity and the tides.

A renewable energy resource is one that is being (or can be) replenished as it is used. The test is replacement keeping pace with use - not the size of the supply, not the price, and not whether the resource is clean.
A resource that is not replenished as it is used, so the supply falls as it is drawn on. Coal, oil, gas and nuclear fuel are non-renewable.
Moving people and goods. Worldwide, transport runs overwhelmingly on oil, as petrol and diesel; bio-fuel and electricity supply smaller shares.
Producing electricity for the mains supply. Almost every resource on the specification's list can be used this way, which is why electricity itself is not a resource.
Warming homes, water and industrial processes. Gas, oil, bio-fuel, geothermal and the Sun are all used for heating directly, without any electricity being generated first.

How dependably a resource can supply energy when it is wanted. Fossil fuels, nuclear fuel and geothermal can be run whenever they are needed; the tides are predictable in advance; wind, the Sun and water waves depend on the weather. Reliability is about availability on demand, not about how much energy the resource gives out.

The damage done by obtaining and using a resource: carbon dioxide from burning fuels, sulfur dioxide leading to acid rain, radioactive waste from nuclear fuel, and land, habitat and landscape effects from dams, wind farms and fuel crops. Every resource has some impact.

concepts.term: Trends in the use of energy resources
concepts.def: Patterns over time, such as the rising share of wind and solar, the decline of coal, and the continued dominance of oil in transport. Trends are driven by cost, by concern about environmental impact and by government decisions.

concepts.term: Political, social, ethical and economic considerations
concepts.def: The non-scientific factors that decide whether an environmental issue is acted on. Science can identify an issue but does not always have the power to deal with it, because cost, jobs, public opinion, fairness between countries and government policy all bear on what is actually done.

mcqs.q: A student is asked to list the main energy resources available for use on Earth. Which list is correct?
options: Nuclear fuel, the tides, geothermal energy and water waves
Bio-fuel, wind, hydro-electricity and mains electricity
Coal, oil, gas and electricity from the mains
The Sun, wind turbines, the tides and bio-fuel crops
mcqs.explain: All four appear in the specification's list of the main energy resources available for use on Earth.

mcqs.q: Where does the energy supplied by a geothermal resource come from?
options: From sunlight that has warmed the ground during the day
From the hot rock lying deep below the Earth's surface
From fossil fuels that are burning deep underground
From fuel steadily burning deep within the Earth
mcqs.explain: Geothermal energy is the energy of hot rock underground, which is why it is available at all hours and in any weather.

mcqs.q: Which statement is the specification's definition of a renewable energy resource?
options: One with a supply so large that it could never all be used up
One that gives off no carbon dioxide while it is being used
One that is being, or can be, replenished as it is used
One that costs nothing to use once it has been built
mcqs.explain: This is the definition word for word: replacement keeping pace with use.

mcqs.q: Nuclear fuel is classified as non-renewable. Which reason for that classification is correct?
options: Uranium is mined from rock, so it is a fossil fuel
Nuclear power stations release carbon dioxide as they run
The clouds from its cooling towers add carbon dioxide
The uranium used is not replenished as it is used
mcqs.explain: Applies the definition directly: the fuel in the ground is not being replaced as it is consumed.

mcqs.q: Why is bio-fuel classified as a renewable energy resource?
options: The crops it is made from can be grown again as the fuel is used
It gives off much less carbon dioxide than burning coal does
There is so much plant material that it could never run out
It is made from living things rather than from rock
mcqs.explain: The definition is met: the supply is replenished, by replanting, at the rate it is drawn on.

mcqs.q: New coal is still slowly forming underground today. Why is coal still classed as non-renewable?
options: It is not: coal is renewable because new coal is still forming
New coal is forming far more slowly than it is being used
Coal gives off carbon dioxide, and renewables are clean
Coal supplies will have run out within about ten years
mcqs.explain: Replenishment has to keep pace with use. Coal takes millions of years to form and is burned in minutes.

mcqs.q: The specification gives three uses of energy resources. Which set of three is correct?
options: Transport, electricity generation and lighting
Electricity generation, heating and cooking food
Transport, electricity generation and heating
Heating, lighting and cooking in the home
mcqs.explain: These are the three uses named in the specification.

mcqs.q: Which energy resource supplies most of the energy used for transport worldwide?
options: Electricity from wind farms
Bio-fuel grown from sugar cane
Coal burned in steam engines
Oil, as petrol and diesel
mcqs.explain: Transport runs overwhelmingly on oil products; other resources supply only small shares.

mcqs.q: Panels on the roof of a house use the Sun to warm the water in a hot water tank. Which use of an energy resource is this?
options: Heating, because the Sun's energy is warming the water directly
Electricity generation, because solar panels make electricity
Transport, because that is a common use of energy
Electricity generation, then heating from the mains
mcqs.explain: The resource is the Sun and the job being done is heating; no electricity is involved at any point.

mcqs.q: Which group of resources is used for all three of transport, electricity generation and heating?
options: Wind, which could drive vehicles, power stations and radiators
Fossil fuels, which are burned for all three of these jobs
The tides, which run at all hours and serve every use
Nuclear fuel, used in stations, cars and in boilers
mcqs.explain: Oil fuels transport, gas and coal generate electricity, and gas and oil heat buildings.

mcqs.q: Why is a wind farm a less reliable energy resource than a gas-fired power station?
options: It is not less reliable, because the wind never stops blowing
Each turbine gives out less energy than a gas power station
Its output falls when the wind drops, whatever the demand
Wind turbines break down far more often than gas plants
mcqs.explain: Reliability is about being available when energy is wanted, and wind output is set by the weather.

mcqs.q: Tidal energy is described as a reliable energy resource. Which statement explains why?
options: The tides are driven by winds that blow daily
Tidal stations give out more energy than any other
The sea is pushed along by winds that never stop
The tides rise and fall on a known cycle
mcqs.explain: The times of high and low water are set by the Moon and the Sun and can be predicted years ahead.

mcqs.q: Which environmental impact arises directly from burning fossil fuels in a power station?
options: Carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide are released into the air
Radioactive waste is produced and has to be stored safely
The steam from the cooling towers poisons nearby land
Acid rain is formed by the carbon dioxide given off
mcqs.explain: Burning releases carbon dioxide, which contributes to global warming, and sulfur dioxide, which causes acid rain.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the environmental impact of renewable energy resources is correct?
options: They cause no environmental damage of any kind at all
They have impacts too, such as land flooded behind a hydro dam
Bio-fuel is the one renewable that has no effect at all on land use
Their only impact is the carbon dioxide released in use
mcqs.explain: Renewable does not mean harmless: dams flood valleys, wind farms alter landscapes and habitats, fuel crops use land.

mcqs.q: The share of UK electricity generated from renewable resources has risen sharply since 2010. Which explanation of this trend is best?
options: The UK's coal, oil and gas have now all been used up
Renewables can now supply power at all times without any backup
Concern about carbon dioxide, and cheaper wind and solar
Fossil fuels have been replaced completely across all energy use
mcqs.explain: Environmental concern plus falling cost is what has driven the change, supported by government policy.

mcqs.q: Scientists identified the harm caused by burning fossil fuels many years ago, yet their use has continued. Which statement best explains this?
options: The evidence is still too uncertain for anyone to act on it
Scientists have not yet explained the harm to any government
No other energy resource could possibly replace the fossil fuels
Political, social, ethical and economic factors count too
mcqs.explain: Science can identify an environmental issue but does not always have the power to deal with it; cost, jobs, public opinion and government policy all bear on what is done.
